title: Augustine, again
tomorrow: Sofia still can't sleep. what does an old book say to keep first?

cards: The decision's made, the message is sent, and somehow you're still awake at two in the morning. A young teacher in Milan knew that feeling. Augustine had the career, the reputation, the life he'd chased.
And he couldn't rest. In his Confessions, he tells how it ended: in a garden, in tears, he hears a child's voice nearby, chanting, take up and read, take up and read.
He opens Paul's letters, reads one passage, and something in him finally goes still.

teach.h: NOT A BETTER JOB OR CITY.
teach.b: So what was he restless for? Not a better job, and not a different city. He'd already tried those.
The answer is the first page of the Confessions, which is a prayer.

In Pusey's translation: "Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee." He wrote that later, as a bishop, looking back over all the running, and he put it on page one.
Augustine's restlessness wasn't a sign that he'd chosen wrong. It was a sign of what he was made for. No career, no city, no person could be big enough to be the resting place.

teach.h: WRITTEN TO GOD, NOT ABOUT HIM.
teach.b: Here's the one to tell a friend: the whole Confessions is written to God, not about him. Augustine tells his life story as a long conversation, and the reader just overhears it.
And the restless heart isn't cured once and for all. It keeps turning toward its rest, the way a compass needle swings back to north.
Until it rests in thee: not a feeling you wait for, but a direction you face.

how: Catholics honor Augustine as a Doctor of the Church and read his Confessions as a prayer; the line about the restless heart is often prayed and quoted, and his feast follows his mother Monica's.

games.q: you're Augustine in the garden, in tears. a child's voice nearby keeps chanting take up and read. what do you do?
o: pick up Paul's letters and read the first passage you see.
go and find out whose child is singing so loudly.
leave the garden and try to sleep it off.
games.why: he opened Paul's letters and read one passage, and in the Confessions he says the restlessness went still.

practice: Close your eyes and let your body get heavy in the chair, shoulders down, hands still. Let whatever is restless in you stay there, without fixing it.
If you pray, you can rest in Augustine's line, our heart is restless until it repose in thee; if not, just let the breathing slow.
